gaps.fact: Germany's climate is cool continental: the Mosel and Franken articles say so, but no chapter of either level names the category and no question asks it.
Gemeinde, the local community or village: the Codex teaches Ort and Ortswein but never gives the word Gemeinde for Germany (its one appearance, i-vbr5xzy6, is Austrian).
Edelfäule means noble rot: it stands only as a pronunciation in the noble-rot technique; no chapter defines it and no question asks it.

Schloss is the German word for castle, the counterpart of château: the rheingau article glosses it once among its labels, and no chapter or question teaches it, though Schloss Johannisberg and Schloss Vollrads are asked.

Of the Court's eleven names only Egon Müller and Joh. Jos. Prüm are ever a key; Dönnhoff (Nahe), Hans Wirsching (Franken), Künstler, Robert Weil and Leitz (Rheingau), Gunderloch (Rheinhessen), Fritz Haag, Dr. Loosen and Selbach-Oster (Mosel) sit in the articles, and Robert Weil, Fritz Haag and Dr. Loosen appear only as wrong options.

The 1971 law established the top two categories, QbA and QmP: QbA appears only in the country ladder and QmP, Qualitätswein mit Prädikat (renamed Prädikatswein from 2007), appears nowhere in the Codex.

Where each German style belongs on a list (dry Riesling with the crisp whites, Kabinett and Spätlese with the off dry, Auslese to Trockenbeerenauslese and Eiswein with the dessert wines) and the serving temperature for each: no question asks it, and the temperature table names no German wine.
Pairings with dry Riesling: the articles give fish, pork, roast chicken and asparagus, but every pairing question is for off dry or sweet Riesling.

courtUpdates.printed: Grosses Gewächs: Single Vineyard Grand Cru Wines; Erstes Gewächs: Single Vineyard Premier Cru Wines
courtUpdates.now: The Thirteenth Ordinance amending the wine rules, approved by the Bundesrat in June 2026 and in force from September 2026, makes the two dry single site terms national: from the 2028 vintage a wine may carry Erstes Gewächs or Grosses Gewächs only from a site classified by a national committee (Komitee Klassifikation Erster und Großer Lagen in Deutschland), not the VDP alone; the same amendment revises Classic. The Codex's c-gswwzvtb still says each region's producers' body decides which sites qualify, which holds until that classification binds. Separately, the Grosslage names carry the word Region from the 2026 vintage under the 2021 law, as the Codex already teaches.
courtUpdates.source: Two searches: the VDP's own statement welcoming the Bundesrat decision on the wine ordinance (vdp.de) and the trade reports of Meininger and Vinetur on the amended Weinverordnung; the details of the Classic change were not found and the dates come from trade reports, so this is medium.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 59 (Germany), Village 37 (Germany), 96 in all. Beyond the map, Producers & Icons asks Egon Müller, Joh. Jos. Prüm and the Fuder, Food & Pairing asks off dry Riesling with Southeast Asian food, and Grapes & Labels asks Weissburgunder. The Introductory column is well served: latitude, rivers, slate, steep slopes, chaptalisation, the four tiers and the six Prädikate in order, Eiswein without botrytis, Mosel villages (Bernkastel, Ürzig, Erden, Wehlen, Piesport), Pfalz, Rheinhessen and Rheingau with Johannisberg. The Certified column is strong on the VDP and its pyramid, the five Certified regions, Oechsle, the Bocksbeutel, halbtrocken and Deutscher Sekt; the thin cells are Gemeinde, Edelfäule, Schloss, QmP, nine of the eleven producers, the list and temperature row and dry Riesling with food. The Village bank leans hard on detail beyond the Court (Gewann, Ortsteil, Weinbergsrolle, Hochgewächs), which does no harm. No factual error found: the Prädikat order, trocken at 4 or 9 grams, halbtrocken at 12 or 18, süss above 45, zone B enrichment of 2 per cent against 3, Eiswein frozen at picking with no legal temperature, Müller-Thurgau from Riesling and Madeleine Royale in 1882, the 1971 law and its five hectare floor, Schloss Johannisberg 1775, the VDP's 1910 founding and its 50 and 60 hectolitre ceilings all hold. One house reading to carry: the Régionale chapters and most Régionale stems are written without diacritics (Spatburgunder, Pradikatswein), a house convention across all 39 Régionale chapters, so it is not logged as an error here. Two searches spent, both on the 2026 amendment of the Weinverordnung.
